questions.A: From this site's own pages, which things can a brand-new visitor try with NO key at all, and which require their own Mistral API key? For each item, give the feature name, the exact page/path to open (as linked from the site), and the key requirement (none vs. own Mistral key). Cover at least: a no-key demo/playground/chat, and any API-calling feature that needs a key.
questions.B: From this site's own pages, what are the recommended first steps for someone who has just opened the site and wants to get hands-on within ten minutes (e.g., quickstart, docs, console, playground)? List the exact page titles and URLs/paths to open, in a sensible first-ten-minutes order, and note any prerequisite each page mentions (sign-up, console login, or an API key).

A.claim: NO KEY REQUIRED — first-call demo on the home page: a brand-new visitor can make a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes with no key at all, by running a model locally on their own laptop with Ollama (the page gives the exact 'ollama pull ministral-3:3b' and curl commands). The same no-key local option is detailed at /demos/on-device.html ("Nothing on this page is sent anywhere."), and the no-key recorded replays are also available at /swarm/ (signed runs replayed in the browser) and /evals/ (published results, read-only).
A.quote: No key needed: a model on your laptop

A.claim: NO KEY REQUIRED — playground/chat-style replay on the team page: a visitor can watch the site's seven-agent team work by replaying recorded runs with no key at all (only giving the conductor a live brief requires a key). Feature: "Replay a recorded run" on the team page.
A.quote: Or replay a recorded run with no key at all.

A.claim: OWN MISTRAL KEY REQUIRED — live team run: to give the seven agents a brief of your own and run them live on Mistral models from your browser, the visitor must supply their own Mistral API key ("Run live on my key"). The same own-key requirement applies to the other API-calling features: /swarm/run.html (run the swarm yourself), /evals/run/ (run the evals in your browser — provider options "Mistral, global endpoint (api.mistral.ai), your key" / "Mistral, EU endpoint (api.eu.mistral.ai), your key"), /demos/side-by-side.html (send one brief to Mistral/OpenRouter — "These demos use your own key, never ours"), and /demos/your-key.html ("Check a key works" sends a real request to the provider). The home page's curl recipe to https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions likewise needs "Authorization: Bearer $MISTRAL_API_KEY" with a key from the Mistral console.
A.quote: A brief of your own (needs your Mistral key)

A.claim: OWN MISTRAL KEY REQUIRED — run the swarm yourself: the swarm runner page runs signed packets of the site's agent swarm live in the visitor's browser, one call at a time, but only on the visitor's own Mistral key (held in tab memory, sent only to api.mistral.ai / api.eu.mistral.ai via POST /v1/chat/completions).
A.quote: Run the swarm yourself, on your own Mistral key

B.claim: The home page is the site's own recommended entry point for a hands-on first ten minutes: its "Start here" section says to pick a path (a local model on your laptop with Ollama, no key, or your own Mistral key), make one call using the built-in "Five minutes to a first call" recipe, then open the demos. The no-key Ollama path has no prerequisite; the Mistral-key path requires getting an API key from the Mistral console first.
B.quote:
Start here
 Pick a path. A model on your laptop with Ollama (no key), or your own Mistral key.
 Make one call. Copy the five-minute recipe below.
 Open the demos. Run the same brief on Mistral beside another model.

B.claim: The dedicated start page (/start/) tells a hackathon participant to open the hackathon briefing — "a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes, with your own key or a local model, then the demos" — so the prerequisite is either your own API key or a local model; it is not needed to read the page itself.
B.quote:
If you are at the hackathon
 Open the hackathon briefing : a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes, with your own key or a local model, then the demos .

B.claim: The demos index (/demos/) is the hands-on hub: everything runs in the browser with no server of the site's and nothing is sent until you press a button that says so — so no sign-up, console login, or API key is needed just to open it. It lists the three demos: "Same brief, three brains" (/demos/side-by-side.html), "Your key, and where it goes" (/demos/your-key.html), and "Level 1, on your device" (/demos/on-device.html).
B.quote: Here you can try it rather than read about it. Everything runs in your browser; there is no server of ours, and nothing is sent anywhere until you press a button that says so.

B.claim: Prerequisites per demo page: Demo 1 "Same brief, three brains" (/demos/side-by-side.html) needs your own keys (Mistral or OpenRouter) for the cloud brains, though a local Ollama model needs no key; Demo 2 "Your key, and where it goes" (/demos/your-key.html) requires an API key obtained from the Mistral console (new accounts start in Free mode, which may train on your calls unless opted out); Demo 3 "Level 1, on your device" (/demos/on-device.html) sends nothing and needs no key. The deeper runners /swarm/run.html ("Run the swarm yourself") and /evals/run/ ("Run the Mistral evals in your browser") each require your own key — Mistral or OpenRouter for evals, or a local Ollama server with no key.
B.quote: Your keys stay in this tab. Each goes only to the provider it belongs to, and only when you press Send. This page has no server and saves nothing.

B.claim: On the key prerequisite specifically: the home page's five-minute recipe says "Get an API key from the Mistral console" before running the curl call with your own key, and warns that Free mode is the default for new accounts with the lowest rate limits; the swarm runner likewise says "Make a key with a low spending limit for demos like this one."
B.quote:
With your own Mistral key
 Get an API key from the Mistral console .
 Put it in your terminal in place of your-key-here , and run the call. Never paste a key into a shared document or a commit.

B.claim: The no-key quickstart path is fully specified on the home page: install Ollama, pull the smallest Ministral 3, and call the local OpenAI-style endpoint — no sign-up, console login, or API key required.
B.quote:
No key needed: a model on your laptop
 Install Ollama .
 Pull the smallest Ministral 3 and call it:
 ollama pull ministral-3:3b
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \

notes: Answers the brief: three first-ten-minutes actions, each labeled no-key vs own-Mistral-key and paired with the page to open (/ , /team/, /team/ + /swarm/run.html).

Every substantive claim carries finding numbers ([1][10], [2], [3][4]) and matches the findings: Ollama/ministral-3:3b/curl no-key first call, no-key recorded replay on /team/, own-key live team run and swarm runner with a Mistral console key.
Word count ~95, well under the 160-word cap.

deliverable.title: Your First Ten Minutes
deliverable.body:
Three things to try in your first ten minutes:

1. Make a first call with no key at all. Open the home page (/), install Ollama, pull ministral-3:3b and run the curl command — nothing leaves your laptop [1][10].

2. Replay the seven-agent team with no key. Open /team/ and choose "Replay a recorded run" [2].

3. Run the team live on your own Mistral key. Open /team/ and select "Run live on my key", or open /swarm/run.html to run the swarm yourself; you need an API key from the Mistral console [3][4].

questions.B: For each of the three features/tools identified for beginners, specify whether they require a key (like an API key) or can be used without one, and clarify if a Mistral key is needed.

A.claim: A hackathon participant can make a first call to a Mistral model in five minutes using a local model with Ollama, requiring no API key.
A.quote:
No key needed: a model on your laptop
 Install Ollama .
 Pull the smallest Ministral 3 and call it:
 ollama pull ministral-3:3b
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model": "ministral-3:3b",
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in five words."}]}'

A.claim: Participants can explore the 'console' design, which allows them to test an OpenAI-style API call with different providers and see what data is sent and to whom.
A.quote:
3 The console
 Playground first
 Pick a provider and see the same OpenAI-style call, and what it sends and to whom.

A.claim: The 'hackathon' design provides a briefing for participants, including how to start, run demos, and share their work in a public repository.
A.quote:
5 The hackathon
 Saturday 21 November 2026 (the home page now)
 The briefing for participants: start here, the three demos, a first call in five minutes, and how to share.

B.claim: The team of AI agents (e.g., conductor, writer, developer) can be used with a Mistral key or replayed without one using recorded runs.
B.quote: Each agent runs under a written behaviour policy, on a Mistral model you choose, called from your browser with your own key. Or replay a recorded run with no key at all.

B.claim: Using Mistral's free mode (or Free mode) requires a Mistral key, but the key's plan determines whether data is used for training or not.
B.quote: There is no separate Free mode key; a key takes the plan of the organization it belongs to.

B.claim: Mistral keys are only sent to Mistral's endpoints (e.g., api.mistral.ai or api.eu.mistral.ai) and are never stored or logged by this site.
B.quote: Your key stays in this tab's memory. It is sent only to the Mistral endpoint you choose below, in the Authorization header of each model call, and is gone when you close the tab. It is never stored, logged or sent to this site.

deliverable.title: Hackathon Quick Start Guide
deliverable.body:
**Quick Hackathon Starter (First 10 Minutes)**

1. **Test a local AI call**
   Open the home page (/). Use Ollama to run `ministral-3:3b`—no key needed. Try the curl command to see it work instantly [1].

2. **Explore API calls in the console**
   Go to /designs/. Pick a provider to see how OpenAI-style calls are sent and where data goes [2].

3. **Review the hackathon design**
   Return to the home page (/). Check the hackathon section for demo ideas, setup steps, and how to share your work publicly [3].
